title: Suicide Prevention in Construction
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: Construction has one of the highest suicide rates of any industry. Learn the warning signs, ask directly, listen, and connect a coworker to help, including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
talking_points: Suicide is the 10th leading cause of death in the U.S., and construction has one of the highest suicide rates of any industry. Knowing the warning signs and how to reach out could save a life.
Warning signs include talking about wanting to die, guilt or shame, or being a burden. Also feeling empty, hopeless, or trapped, or in unbearable pain.
Behavior signs include planning ways to die, withdrawing, saying goodbye, giving away possessions, rage, extreme mood swings, dangerous risks, sleeping or eating more or less, and missing work.
If someone shows these signs, do not ignore them. Start a conversation. The best way to find out if someone is having suicidal thoughts is to ask directly.
Listen without judgment. Express concern and support, and let them know help is available.
Do not tell someone to do it, debate the value of living, or argue that suicide is right or wrong. Never promise to keep their thoughts a secret.
Encourage the person to see a mental health professional, or help them find treatment.

If you or someone you know needs immediate help, call or text 988 (the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline), use the online Lifeline Chat, or text "HOME" to 741741 to reach the Crisis Text Line. Support is free, confidential, and available 24/7. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911 or take them to a nearby emergency room. Stay in touch afterward.
site_hazards_to_check: Coworkers who seem withdrawn, eat lunch alone, or have big changes in mood or behavior
Coworkers who are not following safe practices or are taking dangerous risks
Increased conflict, anger, tardiness, or absences on the crew
No posted or shared crisis line information for the crew
Workers who may not know that 988 and the Crisis Text Line are free and confidential
discussion_questions: What are some warning signs of suicide that you might notice in a coworker?
How would you start a conversation with a coworker you are worried about?
What number do you call or text for immediate help?
